minutes.headline: Select Board reviewed a $13.7M Marshall Park rebuild going to the May 3 town meeting as a debt-exclusion vote.
minutes.summary: The board heard warnings that health insurance renewal costs are up nearly 15% with no relief expected, then reviewed the Parks Commission's Marshall Park renovation proposal (full and a smaller alternative) headed to the May 3 town meeting as a debt exclusion. Most of the meeting was spent line-by-line drafting three new personnel policies (sick leave bank, merit award, gift acceptance), with several open questions left for staff to revise before adoption.

attendees.role: chair of the parks commission, presenter
health plan consultant, Cook and Company, presenter

public_comment.topic: Recognized the passing of a longtime community member, John Latanzi, and his service to town boards.

votes.motion: Approve the weekday entertainment jukebox license and automatic amusement license for Blue Sky Golf/Pal's Golf Lounge LLC as presented
Support the letter, as read and edited by the chair, for the establishment of a satellite emergency facility by UMass Memorial in Groton
Accept the cash donation of $6,900 from Deb and Pete Lincoln for installation of blinds at the Lunenburg Adult Activity Center, under MGL chapter 44 section 53A
Approve the minutes for January 30, 2024, as amended

Enter executive session under MGL chapter 30 section 21A(3) to conduct strategy sessions in preparation for negotiations with non-union personnel, including the police chief, and not to reconvene in open session afterward
votes.outcome: passed 5-0 (roll call: Renee, Tom, Amanda, Michael Ray, chair all voted yes)

budget_items.what_was_said: The clerk noted a Sunday entertainment license, which the applicant did not request, costs more than the weekday one.
The town's insurance broker said Lunenburg's MIIA renewal came in just under the average increase for all MIIA communities, part of a statewide spike in health costs.
A board member noted family health plans are already very expensive before next year's projected increase, calling the trend unsustainable.
The parks commission chair broke out design, permitting and other soft costs for the proposed Marshall Park construction, plus a contingency.
Direct construction, general contractor costs, escalation and design contingency were totaled, with a 5% contingency added.
Soft and hard costs together were presented as the full project cost to be funded.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park debt exclusion tax impact
budget_items.what_was_said: An 18-year amortization was proposed, translating to an added rate per thousand of assessed value and an annual cost to the town's average home.
A member asked about a smaller project option that could be substituted at town meeting, with its own cost and tax impact.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park grants previously secured but relinquished
budget_items.what_was_said: The parks commission previously won two large grants for the full master-plan version but had to decline them when the town couldn't fund the match; officials encouraged reapplication.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park grants still available for the revised project
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair listed grant programs the commission still plans to pursue for the scaled-back project.
The facilities director's maintenance plan showed current spending on the park versus a worst-case estimate of what full new amenities would require annually.

budget_items.topic: State supplemental budget item for Lunenburg schools
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said the House's FY25 supplemental budget included a local earmark intended for Lunenburg public schools, still subject to Ways and Means and conference committee.
The board discussed a one-time monetary award tied to the SAP merit award policy, debating whether it should extend to union employees.
The draft gift policy sets a review/approval threshold between the town manager and select board, and a cap on gifts to individual employees.

budget_items.topic: Lincoln donation for Adult Activity Center blinds
budget_items.what_was_said: A couple donated funds already used to install shades at the Adult Activity Center, requiring retroactive select board acceptance.
The board reviewed and signed an accounts payable warrant; a member suggested publicly stating such totals more often given digital signing.
A member raised switching to a newspaper insert or postcard mailing like another town does, citing the cost of the current mailing.
The draft policy sets contribution and replenishment triggers for the shared sick leave bank in days.

decisions.decision: Apply the merit award policy only to SAP (non-union) employees for this first year, and pursue a warrant article at the fall special town meeting to move it out of the SAP and make it a townwide policy.
Proceed with getting the 56 Cedar Circle ("56 Car A Seller") property professionally appraised before further board action.
Check in with the school committee and finance committee for suggestions before finalizing the recharged budget task force membership.
Draft a three-year lockout on re-enrollment for any employee who withdraws from the sick leave bank program, rather than making enrollment fully irrevocable or a simple annual opt-in/out.
Have town counsel draft the confidentiality/compliance language for sick leave bank committee records rather than relying on the vague 'strictest confidence' wording.

what_happened.line: Select Board reviewed the Marshall Park renovation, headed to a May 3 town meeting vote as a debt exclusion, with the project cost as heard in the recording.
The town's insurance broker said the municipal health plan renewal came in just under the average increase across MIIA communities, part of a statewide spike.
The board spent most of the meeting drafting three new personnel policies -- sick leave bank, merit award, and gift acceptance -- sending open questions back to staff.
The board decided the merit award policy applies only to non-union (SAP) employees this year, with a possible townwide article planned for the fall special town meeting.
The board voted unanimously to accept a cash gift for blinds at the Adult Activity Center and to support a letter backing a satellite emergency facility in Groton.

why_it_matters: If approved at the May 3 town meeting, Marshall Park's cost would be repaid through a debt-exclusion property tax increase, outside the town's normal levy limit.
A larger-than-usual health insurance renewal affects the town's overall budget picture and could add pressure elsewhere as the town builds its next spending plan.
The sick leave, merit award and gift acceptance policies being drafted will set the rules for town employees' benefits and how the town can accept outside donations.
